title: U.S. House · Indiana's 2nd District
area: North-central Indiana, including South Bend, Mishawaka, Elkhart, and Rochester (St. Joseph, Elkhart, Marshall, Fulton, and nearby counties)

context.text: Incumbent Rudy Yakym ran unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary. Jamee Decio won the Democratic primary over Shaun Maeyens. William Henry advanced from the Libertarian Party convention.

candidates.name: Rudy Yakym
candidates.ballotNote: Ran unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary

summary.text: Rudy Yakym is the Republican U.S. Representative for Indiana's 2nd District. A South Bend native and business executive, he worked on the Walorski campaigns before winning the seat in a November 2022 special election after her death. He sits on the House Ways and Means Committee.

background.text: Born February 24, 1984, in South Bend, Indiana; his official biography describes him as a fourth-generation Hoosier raised in South Bend.
Earned an associate degree (2009) and a bachelor's degree (2011) from Indiana University South Bend, and an MBA from the University of Notre Dame (2019).
Worked as a sales manager at the broadband company Omnicity in 2010–11 and was finance director for Rep. Jackie Walorski's congressional campaign in 2011–12.
Was a vice president at the commercial real estate firm Bradley Company from 2013 to 2019; then-Gov. Mike Pence nominated him to the Indiana Judicial Nominating Commission in 2015.
Since 2019 has been director of growth initiatives at Kem Krest, a logistics and supply chain organization, according to his official biography and Wikipedia.

After Walorski died in an August 2022 car accident, he won the Republican nomination by vote of district precinct committee members, on the first ballot in a field of 12, and won the November 8, 2022 special election and the regular election the same day.
Re-elected in 2024 over Democrat Lori Camp and others; unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary.

In the 118th Congress served on the Transportation and Infrastructure and Budget committees; since the 119th Congress serves on Ways and Means (Oversight, Social Security, and Work and Welfare subcommittees).

His official biography cites the Reducing Bureaucracy to Uplift Families Act and the bipartisan Improper Payments Transparency Act as legislation he has championed, and says he helped write the tax portion of the 2025 budget reconciliation law as a Ways and Means member.
Lives in Granger with his wife, Sallyann, and three children, and serves as head usher at New Life Baptist Church, according to his official biography.

priorities.text: Lists 'Securing the Border' among his stated priorities on his official website.
Lists 'Growing Jobs and Wages,' 'Helping Hoosier Farmers,' and 'Putting Your Money Back in Your Pocket' among his stated priorities.
Lists 'Serving Our American Heroes' (veterans) and 'Peace Through Strength' among his stated priorities.

positions.summary: Says he has fought to secure the border, fund the wall, and enforce existing immigration laws, and voted for H.R. 2, the Secure the Border Act.
positions.quote: I've fought to secure the border, give our agents the tools they need, and enforce the laws already on the books. Here's my record: Funded the wall by voting for the One, Big, Beautiful Bill to finish it and give Border Patrol the tools to do the job ... Voted for H.R. 2, the strongest border security bill ever passed by the House

positions.summary: Says he led the fight for the Second Amendment, opposing a gun ban on federal lands and legislation that would strip gun rights during a declared emergency.
positions.quote: Led the fight for the Second Amendment by taking on the gun ban on federal lands and backing legislation to keep the government from stripping gun rights during a declared emergency

positions.summary: Describes himself as a consistent vote and voice against abortion, listing 'the right to life' among rights he says are not up for negotiation.
positions.quote: Fought for the unborn as a consistent vote and voice for life

positions.summary: Says he voted for the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act to lower housing costs by expanding housing supply.
positions.quote: Voted for the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act to lower housing costs by expanding supply and making homeownership affordable again

positions.summary: Says he has stood with Israel against the Iranian regime and its proxies and that the U.S.-Israeli partnership must remain strong.
positions.quote: Stood with Israel against the Iranian regime and its proxies

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Ways and Means (Oversight, Social Security, and Work and Welfare subcommittees) for the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Served on the House Committee on the Budget and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure during the 118th Congress (2023-2024).

candidates.name: Jamee Decio
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary over Shaun Maeyens

summary.text: Jamee Decio is the Democratic nominee for Indiana's 2nd District. An Elkhart native and Notre Dame law graduate, she worked as an Elkhart County deputy prosecutor and attorney and, according to local reports, later lived in California. She is running on affordability, local industry and what her campaign calls protecting democracy.

background.text: Born and raised in Elkhart, Indiana, the daughter of businessman and philanthropist Art Decio (who died in 2020), according to WNDU and her campaign website.

Earned bachelor's and law degrees from the University of Notre Dame; her campaign website says she was among the first 325 women admitted to Notre Dame and one of the first women to graduate from Notre Dame Law.
Worked as an Elkhart County deputy prosecutor and attorney, according to her campaign website; Ballotpedia also lists Elkhart Legal Aid and the Writers Guild of America as affiliations.
Moved to California in her thirties and lived in Los Angeles, working as a lawyer and screenwriter, before returning to northern Indiana to run for Congress.
Her campaign website says she fought through the courts for eight years to adopt her son.
Describes herself as a child advocate and union member; won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary with 72.1% over Shaun Maeyens.

priorities.text: Campaign website cites affordability, saying wages have lagged behind the cost of groceries, medical care, and childcare.
priorities.quote: Jamee recognizes salaries and wages have lagged behind the rising costs of groceries, medical care, and childcare, leaving no room for savings.

priorities.text: Says she wants to eliminate federal economic policies she says jeopardize local jobs, citing the effect of tariffs on Indiana soybean exports to China.
Says she opposes Trump administration redistricting efforts and National Guard/ICE deployments targeting cities with Democratic leaders.

positions.summary: Campaign website says Trump administration tariffs prompted China to impose retaliatory tariffs that hurt Indiana soybean farmers.

candidates.name: William Henry
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Libertarian Party convention on March 22, 2026

summary.text: William Henry is the Libertarian nominee for Indiana's 2nd District. A U.S. Army and Indiana National Guard veteran and communications professional, he has run for office as a Libertarian since 2020, including Lieutenant Governor (2020) and this seat in 2022 and 2024. He says his priorities include government accountability, individual liberty and veterans' issues.

background.text: Born in Indianapolis, Indiana; graduated from Martinsville High School.

Served in the U.S. Army and Indiana Army National Guard from 2005 to 2015, including deployments to Afghanistan and Kuwait, working in military public affairs and journalism; earned the Bronze Star Medal for his journalism work in Afghanistan.
Earned a degree from the U.S. Defense Information School in 2006.

According to his 2024 survey, worked as communications director and later Department Adjutant for The American Legion, Department of Indiana, and has been active with NORML; later worked in communications, public relations and nonprofit advocacy.
Libertarian nominee for Indiana Lieutenant Governor in 2020, receiving 11.4% of the vote.

Sought the Libertarian U.S. Senate nomination in 2022 and lost at the March 5 convention to James Sceniak; ran for the 2nd District seat in the 2022 special and regular elections (about 3.0% in the special) and in 2024.
Describes co-founding Liberty Offense, Inc. and running the Food First Initiative, which he says researches the nutritional properties of hemp.

priorities.text: Cites government accountability and fiscal responsibility as a key campaign message, supporting reduced federal spending and regulatory burdens.
priorities.quote: I support eliminating waste, fraud, and unnecessary bureaucracy; reducing federal spending and regulatory burdens; and limiting government programs that unnecessarily intrude into the lives, property, and finances of Americans.

priorities.text: Cites privacy and limits on government surveillance as a key campaign message, including opposing expanded use of license-plate readers and facial recognition.
Cites a strong national defense while opposing unnecessary foreign entanglements, and says he supports veterans and opposes government taking land for corporate interests such as data centers.

positions.summary: Says taxpayers should not be forced to subsidize projects that primarily benefit corporations, and supports reducing federal spending and regulatory burdens generally.

summary.text: Eric Beebe is an independent candidate for Indiana's 2nd District, a U.S. Army veteran and Purdue Northwest-educated engineer from LaPorte County.

background.text: Born in La Porte, Indiana; earned a bachelor's degree from Purdue Northwest University in 2018.
Served in the U.S. Army from 2009 to 2013.

priorities.text: Says his campaign aims to end unopposed elections and restore competitive democracy in Indiana.
priorities.quote: Every voter deserves a choice. I'm running to end unopposed elections and restore competitive democracy in Indiana.

priorities.text: Says true freedom requires access to healthcare, education, and fair opportunity.
priorities.quote: True freedom requires access to healthcare, education, and fair opportunity. A nation that leaves its people behind cannot call itself free.

priorities.text: Says he supports reasonable term limits for members of Congress.

positions.summary: Says healthcare and education equity are core to his policy priorities, describing them as 'the moral infrastructure of liberty.'
